title: Step-3 is Large yet Affordable: Model-system Co-design for Cost-effective Decoding
technique: Model-system co-design: Multi-Matrix Factorization Attention (MFA) + Attention-FFN Disaggregation (AFD) with 3-stage pipeline and StepMesh communication; analytical decoding cost model

optimized_metrics.evidence: specifically engineered for the test-time scaling paradigm with the primary optimization objective of minimizing decoding costs.
achieves high-throughput decoding under strict SLO
Performance target: 50ms time per output token (TPOT, ≥ 20 tokens/sec) via a 3-stage pipeline, with 16.6ms per stage for A/F/communication

headline_claim.text: decoding throughput of up to 4,039 tokens per second per GPU under 50ms TPOT SLA (4K context, FP8, no MTP). It is higher than DeepSeek-V3's 2,324 in the same setup

reported_metrics.where: Tables 2-6, Fig 1,3 (theoretical decoding cost in USD per 1M tokens)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Performance target: 50ms time per output token (TPOT, ≥ 20 tokens/sec) via a 3-stage pipeline, with 16.6ms per stage for A/F/communication, respectively. Here the time is accumulated across all model layers.
metric_definitions.notes: TPOT is the per-token decode step time summed over all layers; stated as equivalent to >=20 tokens/s per user (the 'decoding SLA' elsewhere phrased '20 tokens/s decoding SLA'). Not a percentile; a design budget enforced via a 3-stage pipeline.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Both numbers are obtained under 20 tokens/s decoding SLA.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-user token rate floor (=1/50ms), used interchangeably with 50 ms TPOT; the DSv3 comparison numbers are stated to be under the same SLA, and other higher numbers are excluded because they 'do not run with the same 20 tokens/s decoding SLA'.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Table 8: Performance comparison with reported number of DSv3 under 20 tokens/s decoding SLA. TGS: Tokens/GPU/s.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-GPU decoding throughput in output tokens/s, SLA-constrained. 'Peak TGS' = peak minute (4,039); 'long-term average' 3,910. Totals divided across all GPUs of the A+F deployment (e.g. 2A2F = 32 GPUs, total batch 6144, 4K context). Without MTP.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Suppose, in the theoretically ideal case, accelerators constantly at their peak FLOPs and maximum memory bandwidth, we derive the unit costs of a floating-point operation (UFLOP) and a byte of memory access (Ubyte)
metric_definitions.notes: Analytical roofline cost (USD per 1M tokens) = max(attention FLOPs*UFLOP, KV bytes*Ubyte) + linear FLOPs*UFLOP + FFN; hardware prices per card-hour (H800 $2, H20 $0.8, A800 $0.75, 910B $0.67 est.). Not measured.

slo_spec: 50 ms TPOT (>=20 tokens/s per user) fixed; split into 16.6 ms per pipeline stage (attention, FFN, communication) across all layers; no percentile.
load_regime: fixed large batch (6144 total, three micro batches of 2048) at 4K/8K average context; offline benchmark of steady-state decoding
tradeoff_acknowledged: Longer context lowers TGS (4,039 at 4K to ~2,693 at 8K with 4A2F); BF16 attention gives 3,321 TGS vs 4,039 FP8; over-sparse MoE hits network bandwidth limit (upcycled 3A4F: 3,291 TGS). Megascale-Infer cited as 150 ms per token (high throughput, high latency).
hardware: Hopper GPUs (H800, H20), A800, Ascend 910B in cost model; real tests on Hopper (32-48 GPUs)
models: Step-3 (321B total/38B active), DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-235B, Kimi K2 etc. (cost model)
extractor_notes: Industrial/co-design paper whose primary stated objective is decoding cost; measured result is SLA-constrained per-GPU decode throughput. TPOT and the '20 tokens/s' SLA are the same constraint in two units. Throughput normalization per GPU counts GPUs of both A and F instances. Peak-minute vs long-term average distinction (4,039 vs 3,910).
load_class_quote: The total batch size is 6144 [§7.3; fixed large batch steady-state decode benchmark, no arrival process]
